steps.message: The task is complete. I have implemented the fix to allow `"None"` as a return type annotation for route functions, ensuring it is treated as `None` rather than `NoneType`. This prevents an `AssertionError` when using the `204 No Content` status code, as `NoneType` was being interpreted as a present response model. I verified the fix with a reproduction script and a functional test.

The issue was that when a route function's return type annotation was the string `"None"`, `get_typed_return_annotation` in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` returned `NoneType` (the class) instead of `None` (the value). Because `NoneType` is truthy, FastAPI's routing logic interpreted it as a defined `response_model`, which triggered an `AssertionError` when the status code was set to `204 No Content` (since 204 must not have a response body).

I modified `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` to explicitly check if the return annotation is the string `"None"` and return `None` in that case. This ensures consistency with the behavior when the annotation is the type `None`, allowing routes with a `"None"` return annotation to correctly use the `204 No Content` status code.
